title: Stir Fried Beef and Vegetables in Soy Sauce

content.title: About
content.content: Beef stir‑fried with vegetables in soy sauce is an Asian‑style dish where tender strips of beef are combined with crisp vegetables (bell pepper, carrot, broccoli, onion) and a savory soy‑based sauce. The high‑heat cooking keeps the meat juicy and the vegetables crunchy.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Soy sauce is traditionally made by fermenting soybeans, wheat and salt.
Stir‑frying uses very high heat for a short time, preserving texture and flavor.
The dish is often served over rice or noodles and garnished with sesame seeds and green onions.
A similar Chinese dish is called "chao rou" (炒肉), while Japanese cuisine features yakitori with vegetables and soy sauce.

items.title: Rich source of protein
items.content: Beef provides high‑quality animal protein essential for muscle growth and repair.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Beef contains vitamin B12, niacin and riboflavin, which support energy metabolism and nervous system health.

items.title: Minerals
items.content: Beef is a good source of iron, zinc and selenium, important for immunity and antioxidant defense.

items.title: Vegetables add fiber and antioxidants
items.content: Broccoli, carrots and bell peppers supply vitamins C, A and dietary fiber that aid digestion.

items.title: Low in carbohydrates
items.content: The dish fits low‑carb diets as the main carbs come from the vegetables.

items.title: High sodium content
items.content: Soy sauce is salty; people with hypertension should choose low‑sodium versions.

items.title: Soy allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to soy products.

items.title: Meat quality
items.content: Use fresh, properly stored beef to avoid foodborne illness.

items.title: Cooking temperature
items.content: Beef should reach an internal temperature of at least 63 °C (145 °F) to kill pathogens.

content.title: How to Cook
content.content: Slice beef thinly, marinate in soy sauce, ginger and garlic for 15‑20 minutes. Heat a wok or large skillet over high heat, stir‑fry the beef quickly, then add the vegetables and cook 3‑5 minutes until crisp‑tender. Finish with a splash of sesame oil, sprinkle sesame seeds and chopped green onions.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store leftovers in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 2‑3 days. Do not freeze the cooked dish, as the vegetables may become soggy.
